On behalf of the YWCA, I'd like to thank you for the opportunity to speak tonight and for considering
the proposed zoning amendment.
For over 110 years, the YWCA Saskatoon has served women and children.
We work tirelessly to move women and their families from a state of surviving to thriving.
We practice under a model of trauma-informed care and meet women where they are at to provide
them with the support they need to recover from trauma, abuse, and countless other obstacles.
The need for our services is increasing steadily.
In 2021, we were forced to turn away 3,721 women and children.
In average of 310 a month, because we simply didn't have room.
We are always full.
In addition, our space is not optimal for providing housing for families with more than two children.
The proposed zoning amendment will allow us to expand, offering 18 units with 28 beds for women
and children needing a safe space to call home.
These 18 self-contained units will be staff 24-7 and provide the supports the families need
to recover and to rebuild.
The proposed expansion is only 2 floors high.
We will be attached to our current building and we will be built on pillars to ensure that parking
will be minimally affected.
We are confident this expansion will have a significant positive impact on the women and children
we serve and on the broader community.
Women prosper, families thrive, and it is a more safe and equitable community for all.
